label: prop-f-ent
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop-f-ent}
Suppose that $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+$ is such that, for some $\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$, one has 
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ and $E(\Psi_+)\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$. Then 
\[
s(\omega_+)=\max\{s(\nu)\mid\nu\in{\mathcal S}_{\omega,\Phi}\}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_{\omega,\Phi}$. Since $E(\Psi_+)\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$, the definition of
${\mathcal S}_{\omega,\Phi}$ and the fact that $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+$ give
\[
\nu(E(\Psi_+))=\omega(E(\Psi_+))=\omega_+(E(\Psi_+)).
\]
By the Gibbs variational principle, $s(\nu)-\nu(E(\Psi_+))\leq P(\Psi_+)$. 
On the other hand, since $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$, $P(\Psi_+)=s(\omega_+)-\omega_+(E(\Psi_+))$. 
Combining the last three relations yields $s(\nu)\leq s(\omega_+)$. 
Since $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_{\omega,\Phi}$, the maximum is attained at
$\omega_+$. \hfill$\Box$
head: manual

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)\cap{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ with
$\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$. If the pair $(\Phi,\Psi_+)$ has the
\textbf{(SD)} property, then $E(\Psi_+)\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dGvp}
Let $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)$ be such that
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ with $[\Psi_+]\in\mathcal{C}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$. Then, one has
\[
\inf_{\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)}s(\omega|\nu)=s(\omega_+)-s(\omega),
\]
and the set of minimizers is precisely ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$.

title: Theorem

Suppose that $d=1$, that $\Phi,\Psi_0\in{\mathcal B}_{\rm f}$,
$\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_0)$, and that $(\omega,\Phi)$ has the property of
finite-range restoration of locality. Then, the following hold:
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item $\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)=\{\omega_+\}$.
\item If $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ with $\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_{\rm f}$, then
$[\Psi_+]\in\mathcal{C}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$.
\item The dynamical Gibbs variational principle holds and $\omega_+$ is its
unique minimizer.
\item $s(\omega_+)>s(\omega)$.
\end{romanenumerate}

are equivalent:
\begin{romanenumerate}

label: prop:vanish_on_average
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We shall use the following notation and properties, $C$ denoting a subset of a Banach space $B$,
and $D$ a subset of its dual $B^\ast$. The annihilators of $C$ and $D$ are, respectively,
\begin{align*}
C^\perp&\coloneq\{f\in B^\ast\mid f(x)=0\text{ for all }x\in C\},\\[4pt]
\leftindex^\perp D&\coloneq\{x\in B\mid f(x)=0\text{ for all }f\in D\}.
\end{align*}
We note that $C^\perp$ is a $\mathrm{w}^\ast\!\!\mathrm{-closed}$ subspace of $B^\ast$ and $\leftindex^\perp D$
a norm-closed subspace of $B$. We recall also that $\leftindex^\perp(C^\perp)$ is the
norm closure of the linear span of $C$ while $(\leftindex^\perp D)^\perp$ is the
$\mathrm{w}^\ast\!\!\mathrm{-closure}$ of the linear span of $D$; see~\cite[Theorem~4.7]{Rudin1973}.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(i)} $\Rightarrow $\textbf{(ii)} For any $A\in{\mathfrak A}$ 
and $a\in{\mathbbm Z}^d$ one has
$$
\left\|m_\Lambda\left(A-\varphi^a(A)\right)\right\|
\le\frac1{|\Lambda|}\sum_{x\in\Lambda\Delta(\Lambda+a)}\|\varphi^x(A)\|
\le\frac{|\Lambda\Delta(\Lambda+a)|}{|\Lambda|}\|A\|=O(|\Lambda|^{-1/d}),
$$
and since $m_\Lambda$ is a linear map such that $\|m_\Lambda(A)\|\le\|A\|$, 
the result follows from an $\epsilon/3$ argument.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)} $\Rightarrow $\textbf{(iii)} Immediately follows 
from the fact that $\varphi(A)=\varphi(m_\Lambda(A))$. 

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iii)} $\Rightarrow $\textbf{(i)} 
By assumption $A\in\leftindex^\perp{\mathfrak A}_I^\ast$. Observing that ${\mathfrak I}_0^\perp\subset{\mathfrak A}_I^\ast$, 
we conclude ${\mathfrak I}=\leftindex^\perp({\mathfrak I}_0^\perp)\supset\leftindex^\perp{\mathfrak A}_I^\ast\ni A$.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iii)} $\Leftrightarrow $ \textbf{(iv)} Since
${\mathfrak A}^\ast_I$ is the linear span of ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$,
one has $\leftindex^\perp{\mathcal S}_I=\leftindex^\perp{\mathfrak A}_I^\ast$.\hfill$\Box$

label: prop:seminorm_interpretation
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:mLambdaDecomp
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}$. On the one hand,
\begin{equation}
m_\Lambda(A)=A+\frac1{|\Lambda|}\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\left(\varphi^x(A)-A\right)=A+A_\Lambda,
\label{eq:mLambdaDecomp}
\end{equation}
where $A_\Lambda\in{\mathfrak I}$. It follows that $\|m_\Lambda(A)\|=\|A+A_\Lambda\|\ge\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/{\mathfrak I}}$, 
and hence
\begin{equation}
\liminf_{\{\Lambda\}}\|m_\Lambda(A)\|\ge\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/{\mathfrak I}}.
\label{eq:overIlow}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, for any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $B_\epsilon\in{\mathfrak I}$ such that 
$\|A-B_\epsilon\|<\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/{\mathfrak I}}+\epsilon$. We deduce that
$$
\|m_\Lambda(A)\|\le\|m_\Lambda(A-B_\epsilon)\|+\|m_\Lambda(B_\epsilon)\|
\le\|A-B_\epsilon\|+\|m_\Lambda(B_\epsilon)\|
\le\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/{\mathfrak I}}+\epsilon+\|m_\Lambda(B_\epsilon)\|,
$$
and hence, by Proposition~\ref{prop:vanish_on_average},
$$
\limsup_{\{\Lambda\}}\|m_\Lambda(A)\|\le\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/{\mathfrak I}}+\epsilon.
$$
Letting $\epsilon\downarrow0$, the last estimate combined with~\eqref{eq:overIlow}
gives~\eqref{eq:overI}.

To prove~\eqref{eq:overIplusR} we derive from~\eqref{eq:mLambdaDecomp}
$$
\|m_\Lambda(A)\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/{\mathbbm R}}=\inf_{b\in{\mathbbm R}}\|A+A_\Lambda-b\mathbbm{1}\|
\ge\inf_{B\in{\mathfrak I},b\in{\mathbbm R}}\|A-B-b\mathbbm{1}\|=\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/({\mathfrak I}+{\mathbbm R})},
$$
and hence
\begin{equation}
\liminf_{\{\Lambda\}}\|m_\Lambda(A)\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/{\mathbbm R}}\ge\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/({\mathfrak I}+{\mathbbm R})}.
\label{eq:overIplusRlow}
\end{equation}
To obtain the opposite estimate, we note that for  any $\epsilon>0$ 
there exists $B_\epsilon\in{\mathfrak I}$ and $b_\epsilon\in{\mathbbm R}$ such that 
$\|A-B_\epsilon-b_\epsilon\mathbbm{1}\|<\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/({\mathfrak I}+{\mathbbm R})}+\epsilon$. It follows that
\begin{align*}
	\|m_\Lambda(A)\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/{\mathbbm R}}
	&=\inf_{b\in{\mathbbm R}}\|m_\Lambda(A-B_\epsilon-b_\epsilon\mathbbm{1})+m_\Lambda(B_\epsilon)+(b_\epsilon-b)\mathbbm{1}\|\\[4pt]
	&\le\inf_{b\in{\mathbbm R}}\left(\|A-B_\epsilon-b_\epsilon\mathbbm{1}\|+\|m_\Lambda(B_\epsilon)\|+|b_\epsilon-b|\right)\\[4pt]
	&\le\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/({\mathfrak I}+{\mathbbm R})}+\epsilon+\|m_\Lambda(B_\epsilon)\|,
\end{align*}
and hence, invoking again Proposition~\ref{prop:vanish_on_average},
$$
\limsup_{\{\Lambda\}}\|m_\Lambda(A)\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/{\mathbbm R}}\le\|A\|_{{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/({\mathfrak I}+{\mathbbm R})}+\epsilon.
$$
Combining this estimate with~\eqref{eq:overIplusRlow} and letting 
$\epsilon\downarrow0$ yields~\eqref{eq:overIplusR}.
\hfill$\Box$

label: prop:ru-R
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:Rtrick
title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)} Setting
$$
T_{X,Y}=\begin{cases*}
	1&\text{if $Y$ is a translate of $X$; }\\[4pt]
	0&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases*}
$$
for $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$, one has
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
	\|R(\Phi)\|\le\sum_{c(X)=0}\|\Phi(X)\|
	&=\sum_{c(X)=0}\frac{1}{|X|}\sum_{x\in X}\|\Phi(X-x)\|
	=\sum_{c(X)=0}\sum_{Y\ni0}\frac{\|\Phi(Y)\|}{|Y|}T_{X,Y}\\[4pt]
	&=\sum_{Y\ni0}\frac{\|\Phi(Y)\|}{|Y|}\sum_{c(X)=0}T_{X,Y}
	=\|\Phi\|_\mathrm{b},
\end{split}
\label{eq:Rtrick}
\end{equation}
where, in the last equality, we used the fact that $Y$ has a unique translate centered 
at $0$. This shows that $R$ is a linear contraction from ${\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ to ${\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}$. Clearly 
$R({\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f})\subset{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}\cap{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$. Moreover, let $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}\cap{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$ and choose a finite set
$Y\supset\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits(A)$ centered at $0$. Define the translation-invariant finite-range
interaction $\Phi_A$ by
\[
\Phi_A(Y+a)=\varphi^a(A),\qquad a\in{\mathbbm Z}^d,
\]
and $\Phi_A(X)=0$ for all other $X\in{\mathcal F}$. Since $Y$ has a unique translate
centered at $0$, $R(\Phi_A)=A$. Moreover, exactly $|Y|$ translates of $Y$ contain
the origin, and hence $\|\Phi_A\|_\mathrm{b}=\|A\|$. Thus,
$R({\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f})={\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}\cap{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$ and for any $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}\cap{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$, one has 
\begin{equation}
\|A\|=\inf\{\|\Phi\|_\mathrm{b}\mid \Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b},R(\Phi)=A\}.
\label{eq:Rbound}
\end{equation}
Now, for any $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}$, there is a sequence $(A_n)_{n\in{\mathbbm N}}$ in ${\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}\cap{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$ 
such that $\sum_n\|A_n\|<\infty$, and $A=\sum_nA_n$. By the above construction,
there is a sequence $(\Phi_n)_{n\in{\mathbbm N}}$ in ${\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ such that 
$R(\Phi_n)=A_n$ and $\|\Phi_n\|_\mathrm{b}=\|A_n\|$ for all $n\in{\mathbbm N}$. It follows that 
$\Phi=\sum_n\Phi_n\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ and $R(\Phi)=A$. 

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)} Repeating the argument in~\eqref{eq:Rtrick}, we derive 
$\omega(R(\Phi))=\omega(E(\Phi))$ for all $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$, and the claim
follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:vanish_on_average}.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iii)} With ${\mathcal K}=\mathop{\mathrm{Ker}}\nolimits(R)$, the quotient ${\mathcal Q}={\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}/{\mathcal K}$ equipped
with the quotient norm $\|\,{\bm\cdot}\,\|_{\mathcal Q}$ is a Banach space. We denote by $\pi$ the
canonical surjection ${\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}\to{\mathcal Q}$. Since ${\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}=\mathop{\mathrm{Ran}}\nolimits(R)$ is closed, the map
$\hat R:\pi(\Phi)\mapsto R(\Phi)$ is an isomorphism, {\sl i.e.,}
a bounded linear bijection from ${\mathcal Q}$ onto ${\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}$, with a bounded inverse. 
For $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$, \eqref{eq:Rbound} can be written 
as
$$
\|\hat R\circ\pi(\Phi)\|=\inf\{\|\Phi+\Psi\|_\mathrm{b}\mid\Psi\in{\mathcal K}\}=\|\pi(\Phi)\|_{\mathcal Q},
$$
and since $\pi({\mathcal B}_f)$ is dense in ${\mathcal Q}$, this identity extends by continuity to $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$.\hfill$\Box$

title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The specific energy observable $E(\Phi)$ is not uniquely
determined by the relation
$$
\omega(E(\Phi))={\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)=\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\tfrac1{|\Lambda|}\omega(H_\Lambda(\Phi)).
$$
There are many $E\in{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}$ for which the equality ${\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)=\omega(E)$ 
holds for all $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$.
\footnote{For example, take $E=E(\Phi)+A$ where $A\in{\mathfrak I}$.} 
This basic observation provides one natural route to the notion
of physical equivalence that will play a central role in this paper.
head: environment

label: rem:fusina
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:fusina}
     
Much more is known about the thermodynamic formalism
and the general structure of ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$. Let us mention the following:
\begin{arabicenumerate} 
\item For any weight $h$, the set $\{\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_h\mid|{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)|=1\}$ 
is residual in ${\mathcal B}_h$, \cite[Theorem~3(3)]{Lanford1968}.

\item On the other extreme, there is a dense subset of ${\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ whose elements
$\Phi$ are such that ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$ contains uncountably many $\varphi$-ergodic
states, \cite[Theorem~V.2.2(c)]{Israel1979}.

\item Although in general the infimum in~\eqref{eq:dual-var} may not be achieved, 
for any weight $h$ the set 
\[
\bigcup_{\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_h}{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)
\]
is {\it norm} dense in ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$, see Observation~3 in the proof 
of~\cite[Theorem~6.2.44]{Bratteli1981}. 

\item For any finite set $S=\{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_N\}$ of $\varphi$-ergodic 
elements of ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ with finite specific entropy, there exists $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ such 
that $S$ is contained in the set of $\varphi$-ergodic elements of ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$, 
\cite[Theorem~V.2.2(a)]{Israel1979}.
\end{arabicenumerate}

label: prop:two-rpe
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:two-rpe} 
Let $\Phi,\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ and $c\in{\mathbbm R}$. Then the following statements are equivalent.
\begin{romanenumerate} 
\item $\Phi-\Psi\in R^{-1}({\mathfrak I}+c\mathbbm{1})$.
\item 
\[
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\left(m_\Lambda(E(\Phi))-m_\Lambda(E(\Psi))\right)=c\mathbbm{1}.
\]
\item
\[
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}(H_\Lambda(\Phi)-H_\Lambda(\Psi))=c\mathbbm{1}.
\]
\item For any $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$, 
$$
{\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)-{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega)=c.
$$
\item For any $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$, 
\[
\omega(E(\Phi))-\omega(E(\Psi))=c.
\]
\end{romanenumerate}
Moreover, any of these statements implies $P(\Psi)-P(\Phi)=c$ and ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$.

label: eq:octopus
title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(ii)} This is a direct consequence of 
Propositions~\ref{prop:vanish_on_average}(i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) and~\ref{prop:ru-R}(ii).

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(iii)}
We first establish the estimate
\begin{equation}
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\left\|\frac1{|\Lambda|}H_\Lambda(\Theta)-m_\Lambda(E(\Theta))\right\|=0
\label{eq:octopus}
\end{equation}
for every $\Theta\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$. Suppose first that $\Theta\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ and that
$\Theta(X)=0$ for $\oslash(X)>r$. For $\Lambda\in{\mathcal F}$,
$$
\sum_{X\subset\Lambda}\Theta(X)-\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\varphi^x\left(\sum_{X\ni0}\frac{\Theta(X)}{|X|}\right)
=-\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\cap\Lambda^c\neq\emptyset}{X\ni x}}\frac{\Theta(X)}{|X|}.
$$
Hence, setting $\Lambda_r=\{x\in\Lambda\mid\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(x,\Lambda^c)>r\}$,
\[
\left\|\frac1{|\Lambda|}H_\Lambda(\Theta)-m_\Lambda(E(\Theta))\right\|
\leq\frac{|\Lambda\setminus\Lambda_r|}{|\Lambda|}\|\Theta\|_\mathrm{b},
\]
and~\eqref{eq:octopus} follows along centered cubes. For general
$\Theta\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$, choose $\Theta_n\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ with
$\|\Theta_n-\Theta\|_\mathrm{b}\to0$. Since, uniformly in $\Lambda$,
\[
\left\|m_\Lambda(E(\Upsilon))\right\|\leq\|\Upsilon\|_\mathrm{b},
\qquad
\frac1{|\Lambda|}\|H_\Lambda(\Upsilon)\|\leq\|\Upsilon\|_\mathrm{b},
\]
the finite-range estimate extends to $\Theta$.

Taking $\Theta=\Phi-\Psi$ in~\eqref{eq:octopus},
condition~\textbf{(ii)} yields~\textbf{(iii)}.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iii)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(iv)} is an immediate consequence of Theorem~\ref{thm:Gibbs}(i).

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iv)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(v)} is a consequence of Definition~\eqref{def:tpe}.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(v)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(i)} Invoking Propositions~\ref{prop:ru-R}~\textbf{(ii)}
and~\ref{prop:vanish_on_average}~\textbf{(i)} $\Rightarrow$~\textbf{(iv)} gives that $\omega(R(\Phi))-\omega(R(\Psi))=c$
for all $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$. The claim now follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:vanish_on_average}~\textbf{(iv)} $\Rightarrow$~\textbf{(i)}. 

\medskip\noindent The last statement follows from Part~(iv) and the Gibbs variational principle~\eqref{eq:GibbsPrince}.
\hfill$\Box$

title: Definition
body_md:
Two interactions $\Phi,\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ are called
\textsl{physically equivalent,} written $\Phi\sim\Psi$, if
\[
R(\Phi-\Psi)\in{\mathfrak I}+{\mathbbm R}\mathbbm{1}.
\]
They are called \textsl{strongly physically equivalent,} written
$\Phi\approx\Psi$, if
\[
R(\Phi-\Psi)\in{\mathfrak I}.
\]
These are equivalence relations compatible with the vector space structure of
${\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Equivalently, $\Phi\sim\Psi$ iff
$\Phi\equiv\Psi\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{\mathcal I}+{\mathcal R})$, and
$\Phi\approx\Psi$ iff $\Phi\equiv\Psi\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{\mathcal I})$.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:RuIso}, the same notation will be used for the induced
equivalence relations modulo ${\mathfrak I}+{\mathbbm R}\mathbbm{1}$ and modulo ${\mathfrak I}$ on
${\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}$. Proposition~\ref{prop:two-rpe} shows, in particular, that physical
equivalence is precisely equality of the specific energy functionals up to an
additive constant.

label: prop:physeq
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:physeq} 
If $\Phi\sim\Psi$, then for any $t\in[0,1]$, 
\[
P((1-t)\Phi+t\Psi)=(1-t)P(\Phi)+tP(\Psi). 
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:two-rpe}(iv), there is $c\in{\mathbbm R}$ such
that ${\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega)-{\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)=c$ for all $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$.
The last assertion of Proposition~\ref{prop:two-rpe} gives
$P(\Psi)-P(\Phi)=-c$. Hence, by the Gibbs variational principle,
\[
\begin{split}
P((1-t)\Phi+t\Psi)
&=\sup_{\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}}
\big(s(\omega)-{\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)-t({\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega)-{\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega))\big)\\
&=P(\Phi)-tc=(1-t)P(\Phi)+tP(\Psi).
\end{split}
\]
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:Pafin
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(ii)} Choose
$\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}((\Phi+\Psi)/2)$. By \textbf{(i)} and the
linearity of the specific energy in the interaction,
\[
s(\omega)=\frac12\big({\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)+P(\Phi)\big)
+\frac12\big({\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega)+P(\Psi)\big).
\]
The variational principle gives
$s(\omega)\leq{\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)+P(\Phi)$ and
$s(\omega)\leq{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega)+P(\Psi)$.
Hence both inequalities are equalities, and
$\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)\cap{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$.


\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(i)} Let $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)\cap{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$. 
Then the relations 
\[
s(\omega)={\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)+P(\Phi),\qquad s(\omega)={\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega)+P(\Psi),
\]
give that, for $t\in[0,1]$, 
\[
s(\omega)=(1-t)s(\omega)+ts(\omega)={\mathcal e}_{(1-t)\Phi+t\Psi}(\omega)+(1-t)P(\Phi)+tP(\Psi).
\]
This equality and the dual variational principle, Theorem~\ref{thm:Gibbs}~\textbf{(iv)}, yield that 
\[
(1-t)P(\Phi)+tP(\Psi)\leq P((1-t)\Phi+t\Psi).
\]
The opposite inequality follows from the convexity of the pressure and~\textbf{(i)} follows. \hfill$\Box$

label: def:wg
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:wg}
A state $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ is called \textsl{weak Gibbs} for the
interaction $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ if there exist constants $c_\Lambda>0$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac{c_\Lambda}{|\Lambda|}=0,
\label{eq:mil-er}
\end{equation}
and such that, for all $\Lambda$,
$$
\mathrm{e}^{-c_\Lambda}\omega_{\Phi,\Lambda}^\mathrm{c}\leq\omega_\Lambda\leq \mathrm{e}^{c_\Lambda} \omega_{\Phi,\Lambda}^\mathrm{c}.
$$
$\omega$ is called \textsl{log weak Gibbs} for $\Phi$ if there exist
constants $c_\Lambda >0$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:mil-er} and such that, for all
$\Lambda$,
$$
- c_\Lambda+\log \omega_{\Phi,\Lambda}^\mathrm{c}\leq\log\omega_\Lambda
\leq c_\Lambda+\log\omega_{\Phi,\Lambda}^\mathrm{c}.
$$
We denote by ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{wg}(\Phi)$ the set of all weak Gibbs states for
$\Phi$, and by ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{lwg}(\Phi)$ the set of all log weak Gibbs states.

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)} For $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{s}$, we have
\begin{align*}
\|W_\Lambda(\Phi)\|
&\leq\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\cap\Lambda\neq\emptyset}{X\cap\Lambda^c\neq\emptyset}}\|\Phi(X)\|
\leq\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\ni x}{X\cap\Lambda^c\neq\emptyset}}\|\Phi(X)\|\\
&=\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\ni0}{(X+x)\cap\Lambda^c\neq\emptyset}}\|\Phi(X)\|\\
&=\sum_{X\ni0}\|\Phi(X)\|
\left|\left\{x\in\Lambda\mid(X+x)\cap\Lambda^c\neq\emptyset\right\}\right|\\
&\leq|\Lambda|\sum_{X\ni0}\|\Phi(X)\|
=|\Lambda|\,\|\Phi\|_\mathrm{s}.
\end{align*}

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)} Dividing the preceding estimate before its last
inequality by $|\Lambda|$ gives
\[
\frac1{|\Lambda|}\|W_\Lambda(\Phi)\|
\leq\sum_{X\ni0}\|\Phi(X)\|
\frac{\left|\left\{x\in\Lambda\mid(X+x)\cap\Lambda^c\neq\emptyset\right\}\right|}{|\Lambda|}.
\]
For fixed $X\ni0$, the set in the numerator is contained in
\[
\left\{x\in\Lambda\mid\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}\nolimits(x,\Lambda^c)\leq\oslash(X)\right\}.
\]
Its relative cardinality therefore tends to zero along every van~Hove net,
while it is bounded by one. Since
$\sum_{X\ni0}\|\Phi(X)\|=\|\Phi\|_\mathrm{s}<\infty$, dominated convergence
yields Part~\textbf{(ii)}.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iii)} Part~\textbf{(ii)} applies in particular along
centered cubes, and the assertion follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:Abel} and
$U_\Lambda(\Phi)=H_\Lambda(\Phi)+W_\Lambda(\Phi)$. \hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: thm:deltaPhi
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:deltaPhi}
The derivation $\delta_\Phi$ is norm-closable on ${\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$.\footnote{We will always 
denote its closure by the same letter.} Its closure generates a $C^\ast$-dynamics 
$\tau_\Phi$ on ${\mathfrak A}$ if and only if $(\mathrm{Id}\pm\delta_\Phi){\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$ is dense in ${\mathfrak A}$. 
In this case, for all $A\in{\mathfrak A}$, 
\[
\tau_\Phi^t(A)=\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} tH_\Lambda(\Phi)}A \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} tH_\Lambda(\Phi)},
\]
and the limit is uniform for $t$ in compact subsets of\/ ${\mathbbm R}$.
head: environment

label: thm:KMSeq
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:KMSeq} 
For $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$, 
\[ 
{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{KMS}(\Phi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi).
\]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The classical results in~\cite[Propositions~6.2.41 and~6.2.42]{Bratteli1981}
yield ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{KMS}(\Phi)\subset{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$, with  equality 
established only in the case where $\Phi$ is in the space ${\mathcal B}^r$ defined in
Section~\ref{sec:exp-dec} below. The equality in the case $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$ 
is a consequence of~\cite[Theorems~A and~B]{Araki2003}.
head: environment

label: thm:phys-eq
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:phys-eq} 
Suppose that $\Phi,\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$. Then the following statements 
are equivalent: 
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item $\Phi\sim\Psi$. 
\item For any $t \in [0,1]$, 
\[ P((1-t)\Phi+t \Psi)=(1-t)P(\Phi) + t P(\Psi). \]
\item ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)\cap{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)\neq\emptyset$.
\item $\tau_\Phi=\tau_\Psi$. 
\item ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$.
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(ii)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(iii)} Follow from 
Propositions~\ref{prop:physeq} and~\ref{prop:Pafin} respectively.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iii)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(iv)} By Theorem~\ref{thm:KMSeq}, there is a state in ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$
which is $1$-KMS for $\tau_\Phi$ and $\tau_\Psi$. Theorem~\ref{thm:israel}~\textbf{(iii)}
implies $\tau_\Phi=\tau_\Psi$.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(iv)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(v)} Follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:KMSeq}.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(v)}$\Rightarrow$\textbf{(i)} Clearly~\textbf{(v)}$\Rightarrow$~\textbf{(iii)} $\Rightarrow$~\textbf{(iv)}, 
so the claim reduces to~\textbf{(iv)} $\Rightarrow$~\textbf{(i)}. Since $\delta_\Phi=\delta_\Psi$, invoking Theorem~\ref{thm:deltaPhi} it suffices 
to show that any $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$ such that
\begin{equation}
\sum_{X\in{\mathcal F}}[\Phi(X),A]=0
\label{eq:paperlog}
\end{equation}
for all $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$ satisfies $\Phi\in{\mathcal I}+{\mathcal R}$. Now, for $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\Lambda$, we
can rewrite~\eqref{eq:paperlog} as $\left[U_\Lambda(\Phi),A\right]=0$. Taking the partial normalized trace over ${\mathfrak A}_{\Lambda^c}$ and using the
triviality of the center of ${\mathfrak A}_\Lambda$, we obtain
\[
H_\Lambda(\Phi)+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits_{\Lambda^c}(W_\Lambda(\Phi))=c_\Lambda\mathbbm{1}
\]
for some $c_\Lambda\in{\mathbbm R}$. Hence, by Proposition~\ref{prop:BsStuf}(ii)--(iii),
for any $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$,
\[
\omega(E(\Phi))=\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac{c_\Lambda}{|\Lambda|}\eqcolon c,
\]
and the claim follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:two-rpe}.\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: thm:energyp
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:energyp}
Suppose that $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$. Then
$$
{\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)={\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)
$$
holds for all $t\in{\mathbbm R}$ and $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$.
head: environment

label: prop:energy-monotonicity
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:energy-monotonicity}
Suppose that $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$ is such that $\tau_\Phi$ preserves the specific
entropy, and let $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$ for some $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$. Then, for all
$t\in{\mathbbm R}$,
\[
{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)\geq {\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega).
\]
Consequently, for every $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)$,
\[
{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega_+)\geq {\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The Gibbs variational principle and conservation of the specific entropy give
\[
0\leq
-s(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)
+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)+P(\Psi)
=
{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)-{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega),
\]
where in the last equality we used $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$. Hence
\[
{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\overline\omega_T)\geq{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega)
\]
for all $T>0$. The last assertion follows by weak-$^\ast$ continuity of
${\mathcal e}_\Psi$. \hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: thm:first-s
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:first-s}
If $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^r$, then: 
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$ and Theorems~\ref{thm:KMSeq}, \ref{thm:phys-eq} and~\ref{thm:energyp} apply. 
\item For all $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$ the map ${\mathbbm R}\ni t\mapsto\tau_\Phi^t(A)$
has an analytic extension to the strip $|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|<r/2\|\Phi\|_r$, and for any 
$z$ in this strip, 
\[
\|\tau_\Phi^z(A)\|\leq\|A\|\mathrm{e}^{r|\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nolimits(A)|}\frac{r}{r- 2\|\Phi\|_r|\mathop{\mathrm{Im}}\nolimits z|}.
\]
\item If $r>\log\mathop{\mathrm{dim}}\nolimits{\mathcal H}$ and $\|\Phi\|_r<\frac1{2\mathop{\mathrm{dim}}\nolimits{\mathcal H}}$, then ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$ is a singleton, 
so that ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{wg}(\Phi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{lwg}(\Phi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$. 
\item If $\|\Phi\|_r<r$, then ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{wg}(\Phi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{lwg}(\Phi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$. 
\item $s(\omega)=s(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)$ for all $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$. 
                                                                                                  
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

label: thm:pres-law
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:pres-law}
Let $(\omega,\Psi)$ be a regular pair such that either
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item $\|\Psi\|_r<r$ for some $r>0$, or
\item $d=1$ and $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$.
\end{romanenumerate}
Let $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ and $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$. Then there exists $T>0$ such that, for $|t|<T$, the specific relative
entropy of $\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t$ with respect to
$\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t$ exists and satisfies
$$
s(\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t|\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)=s(\nu|\omega).
$$
One can take $T=\infty$ in case $\mathrm{(ii)}$ or if $\omega$ is $\tau_\Phi$-invariant.
head: environment

label: thm:second-s
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:second-s}
Suppose that $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}^{\oslash^{r}}$. 
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item If $r>d$, then $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$, and
Theorems~\ref{thm:KMSeq} and~\ref{thm:phys-eq} apply. 
\item If $d=1$ and $r\geq1$, then ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$ is a singleton. 
\item If $r>2d$, then
\[
s(\omega)=s(\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)
\]
for all $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$.
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)} This follows from~\cite[Theorem~4.8]{Bru2017}.

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{(ii)} If $d=1$ and $r\geq1$, then
\[
\sum_{X\ni0}\oslash(X)\|\Phi(X)\|
\leq
\sum_{X\ni0}|X|(1+\oslash(X))^r\|\Phi(X)\|
=
\|\Phi\|_{\oslash^r}<\infty.
\]
The one-dimensional uniqueness theorem of Araki~\cite{Araki1975},
see also~\cite[Theorem~IV.6.1]{Simon1993}, therefore yields that
${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$ is a singleton.

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{(iii)} See the companion paper~\cite{Jaksic2026b}.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: thm:pre-ara
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:pre-ara}
Suppose that $d=1$. For any $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$, ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{wg}(\Phi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{lwg}(\Phi)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$ is a singleton.
head: environment

label: thm:pres-law-1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:pres-law-1}
Suppose that $d=1$ and $\Psi,\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$. If the pair $(\omega,\Psi)$ is regular
then, for all $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$, $s(\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t|\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^t)$ 
exists and does not depend on $t$.
head: environment

label: thm-qstein
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm-qstein}
Suppose that $\Phi, \Psi\in {\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$, and that $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Phi)$, $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$. 
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item If $d=1$, then the limit~\eqref{eq:lim} exists for all $\alpha\in{\mathbbm R}$, and the 
function $e$ is real analytic on ${\mathbbm R}$. Moreover, $e^\prime(0)<e^\prime(1)$ 
iff\, $\Phi\not\sim\Psi$. If $\Phi\sim\Psi$, then $e$ vanishes identically on ${\mathbbm R}$.
\item If $d>1$, then for any $a>1$ there is $\delta>0$ such that if 
$\|\Phi\|_\mathrm{s}<\delta$ and $\|\Psi\|_\mathrm{s}<\delta$, then 
the limit~\eqref{eq:lim} exists for all $\alpha\in(-a,a)$, and the function 
$e$ is real analytic on this interval. Moreover, $e^\prime(0)<e^\prime(1)$ iff $\Phi\not\sim\Psi$. 
If $\Phi\sim\Psi$, then $e$ vanishes identically on $(-a,a)$.
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

label: thm:jpt-o
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
In~\cite{Jaksic2023a} the strict statement was proven under the
assumption that $\Phi,\Psi\in{\mathcal B}^r$ and that $(\omega,\Psi)$ is regular. The proof
extends to $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$ and $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$, assuming conservation of the specific
entropy. The proof below also dispenses with the regularity assumption.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(T_n)_{n\in{\mathbbm N}}$ be such that $\overline\omega_{T_n}\to\omega_+$. By the
Gibbs variational principle and~\eqref{eq:baromegaTconserv},
\begin{align*}
0
&\leq -s(\overline\omega_{T_n})+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\overline\omega_{T_n})+P(\Psi)\\
&=-s(\omega)+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\overline\omega_{T_n})+P(\Psi)\\
&={\mathcal e}_\Psi(\overline\omega_{T_n})-{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega).
\end{align*}
Since ${\mathcal e}_\Psi$ is $\mathrm{w}^\ast\!\!\mathrm{-c}$ontinuous, letting $n\to\infty$ gives ${\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega_+)\geq{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega)$,
which proves Part~\textbf{(i)}.

Suppose now that equality holds. Then
\[
-s(\overline\omega_{T_n})+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\overline\omega_{T_n})+P(\Psi)\rightarrow0.
\]
The map $\nu\mapsto -s(\nu)+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\nu)+P(\Psi)$
is $\mathrm{w}^\ast\!\!\mathrm{-l}$ower semicontinuous. Hence
\[
0\leq -s(\omega_+)+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega_+)+P(\Psi)\leq0,
\]
and therefore $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$. If
${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)=\{\omega\}$, then $\omega_+=\omega$, contradicting the standing
assumption that $\omega$ is not $\tau_\Phi$-invariant. This proves
Part~\textbf{(ii)}. \hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: thm:GibbsII
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)} The tracial state on ${\mathfrak A}$ is the unique maximizer of the
specific entropy $s$, \cite[Theorem~IV.2.4]{Simon1993}. Thus setting $e_0=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits(E(\Phi))$,
we have ${\mathcal s}(e_0)=\max\{s(\nu)\mid\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}\}=\log\mathop{\mathrm{dim}}\nolimits{\mathcal H}$. The function $\beta_\ast={\mathcal s}'$
being monotone decreasing, we have $\beta_\ast(e)\ge0$ for $e\in[e_\mathrm{min},e_0]$,
and $\beta_\ast(e)\le0$ for $e\in[e_0,e_\mathrm{max}]$.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)}
Since $\hat{\mathcal s}$ is convex, it is the Legendre--Fenchel transform of ${\mathcal p}$, 
which translates into Relation~\eqref{eq:smalldualGibbs}.
A well known property of the Legendre--Fenchel 
transform~\cite[Theorem~23.5]{Rockafellar1970},\footnote{$(\partial f)(x)$ 
denotes the subdifferential of $f$ at $x$, \textsl{i.e.,\ } the interval 
$[(\partial^-f)(x),(\partial^+f)(x)]$.}
$$
-e\in(\partial{\mathcal p})(\beta)
\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad {\mathcal p}(\beta)-{\mathcal s}(e)=-\beta e
\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad\beta=\beta_\ast(e),
$$
yields Relation~\eqref{eq:AizLieb}. Finally, it follows from definition~\eqref{eq:csDef}
that $s(\nu)\le{\mathcal s}(e)$ for any $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ such that ${\mathcal e}_\Phi(\nu)=e$,
and Relation~\eqref{eq:AizLieb} yields that
$$
s(\nu)={\mathcal s}(e)={\mathcal p}(\beta_\ast(e))+\beta_\ast(e)e=P(\beta_\ast(e)\Phi)+\beta_\ast(e){\mathcal e}_\Phi(\nu)
$$
iff $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\beta_\ast(e)\Phi)$.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:st-pres
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\textbf{(i)} Since ${\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)={\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega_\mathrm{eq})$, the dual variational 
principle~\eqref{eq:dual-var} gives
$$
s(\omega)=\inf_{\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}}\left(P(\Psi)+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega)\right)\leq
P(\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi)+\beta_\mathrm{eq}{\mathcal e}_{\Phi}(\omega_\mathrm{eq})=s(\omega_\mathrm{eq}),
$$ 
with equality iff $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi)$. If $\beta_\mathrm{eq}\neq0$,
such a state is $\tau_\Phi$-invariant since it is invariant under
$\tau_{\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi}^t=\tau_\Phi^{\beta_\mathrm{eq} t}$. If $\beta_\mathrm{eq}=0$, it is the
tracial state and is again $\tau_\Phi$-invariant. Both cases contradict our
standing assumption.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{(ii)} For all $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ such that 
${\mathcal e}_\Phi(\nu)={\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)\eqcolon e_\ast$ we have, by~\eqref{eq:smalldualGibbs}
and the variational definition of ${\mathcal s}$,
$$
s(\omega_\mathrm{eq})=P(\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi)+\beta_\mathrm{eq}{\mathcal e}_{\Phi}(\omega)
={\mathcal p}(\beta_\mathrm{eq})+\beta_\mathrm{eq} e_\ast={\mathcal s}(e_\ast)\ge s(\nu),
$$
with equality iff $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\omega,\Phi)$. By the second identity 
in~\eqref{eq:omegaplusprop}, this applies to $\nu=\omega_+$.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

title: Definition
body_md:
An observable $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}$ is called a \textsl{constant of the motion} of $\tau_\Phi$ if
\[
\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t(A)=\nu(A)
\]
for all $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$, equivalently if ${\mathcal T}_\Phi(A)={\mathbbm R}$.
We denote by
\[
{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)
\coloneq
\left\{[A]\coloneq A+{\mathfrak I}+{\mathbbm R}\mathbbm{1}\mid {\mathcal T}_\Phi(A)={\mathbbm R}\right\}
\subset {\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{sa}/({\mathfrak I}+{\mathbbm R}\mathbbm{1})
\]
the corresponding space of constants of the motion modulo physical
equivalence.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
An interaction $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ is said to be $\tau_\Phi$-\textsl{invariant} if its 
specific energy observable $E(\Psi)$ is a constant of the motion. We denote by
\[
{\mathcal C}(\Phi)\coloneq
\left\{[\Psi]\coloneq\Psi+{\mathcal I}+{\mathcal R}\mid \Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b},[E(\Psi)]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)\right\}
\subset{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}/({\mathcal I}+{\mathcal R})
\]
the quotient space of physical equivalence classes of $\tau_\Phi$-invariant interactions.
head: environment

label: prop:CMlevels
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:CMlevels}
The map
\[
{\mathcal C}(\Phi)\ni[\Psi]\longmapsto [E(\Psi)]
\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)
\]
is an isometric isomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:ru-R}(ii), $E(\Psi)\equiv R(\Psi)$ (mod ${\mathfrak I}$). 
The assertion is therefore the restriction of the second isometric
isomorphism of Theorem~\ref{thm:RuIso} to the subspaces singled out by the
conservation law.\vskip-8pt\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: SD
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{SD}
We say that the pair $(\Phi,\Psi)\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}\times{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$ has the \textbf{(SD)}\footnote{SD stands for surface-dynamics.}
property if the following hold for all $t$ in a neighborhood of $0$.
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item For every finite $\Lambda\in{\mathcal F}$, the surface energy
\[
W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)
=
\lim_{\widetilde\Lambda}
\big(H_{\widetilde\Lambda}(\Psi|\Phi,t)-H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)
-H_{\widetilde\Lambda\setminus\Lambda}(\Psi|\Phi,t)\big)
\]
exists in norm, where $\widetilde\Lambda$ runs over the finite supersets of
$\Lambda$, directed by inclusion.
\item The surface energies vanish in the van Hove sense,
\[
\lim_\Lambda\frac{1}{|\Lambda|}\|W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\|=0.
\]
\item One has, again in the van Hove sense,
\[
\lim_\Lambda\frac1{|\Lambda|}\left\|\tau_\Phi^{-t}(H_\Lambda(\Psi))-H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)\right\|=0.
\]
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

label: eq:DynCommut
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: eq:Borodin
title: Proof
body_md:
Since
\[
\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} sH_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)}
=\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} tH_\Lambda(\Phi)}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} sH_\Lambda(\Psi)}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} tH_\Lambda(\Phi)},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} sH_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)}A\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} sH_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)}
=\tau_\Phi^{-t}\circ \tau_\Psi^s\circ \tau_\Phi^{t}(A)
\label{eq:Borodin}
\end{equation}
for all $A\in{\mathfrak A}$, uniformly for $s$ and $t$ in compacts. Our assumption~\eqref{eq:DynCommut} 
yields that the right-hand side of the last identity is just $\tau_\Psi^s(A)$. 
Since $[H_{\Lambda^\prime\setminus\Lambda}(\Psi|\Phi,t),A]=0$ whenever $A\in{\mathfrak A}_\Lambda$, 
the \preSD{} property further gives that, for such $A$ and all $t$ in a neighborhood of $0$,
\[
\lim_{\Lambda^\prime}[ H_{\Lambda^\prime}(\Psi|\Phi,t),A]
=[H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)+W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t),A].
\]
Hence, on the one hand
\begin{align*}
\tau_\Psi^s(A)
&=\lim_{\Lambda^\prime}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} sH_{\Lambda^\prime}(\Psi|\Phi,t)}A\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} sH_{\Lambda^\prime}(\Psi|\Phi,t)}\\[4pt]
&=A+\mathrm{i}\,\lim_{\Lambda^\prime}\int_0^s\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i} uH_{\Lambda^\prime}(\Psi|\Phi,t)}
[H_{\Lambda^\prime}(\Psi|\Phi,t),A]\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i} uH_{\Lambda^\prime}(\Psi|\Phi,t)}\mathrm{d} u\\[4pt]
&=A+\mathrm{i}\int_0^s\tau_\Psi^u([H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)+ W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t),A])\mathrm{d} u,
\end{align*}
and on the other hand
\[
\tau_\Psi^s(A)=A+\mathrm{i}\int_0^s\tau_\Psi^u([H_\Lambda(\Psi)+W_\Lambda(\Psi),A])\mathrm{d} u,
\]
which allows us to conclude that
\[
[H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)+ W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t),A]=[H_\Lambda(\Psi)+W_\Lambda(\Psi),A].
\]
Taking the partial normalized trace over ${\mathfrak A}_{\Lambda^c}$ yields
\[
[ H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)-H_\Lambda(\Psi)+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits_{\Lambda^c}(W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)-W_\Lambda(\Psi)),A]=0, 
\]
and so 
\begin{equation}
H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)-H_\Lambda(\Psi)+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits_{\Lambda^c}(W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)-W_\Lambda(\Psi))=C_\Lambda(t)\mathbbm{1}
\label{eq:sosot}
\end{equation}
for some $C_\Lambda(t)\in{\mathbbm R}$. Since $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits(H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)-H_\Lambda(\Psi))=0$, we deduce
\[
\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits(W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)-W_\Lambda(\Psi))=C_\Lambda(t).
\]
Hence, by Proposition~\ref{prop:BsStuf}(ii) and the \preSD{} property,
\[
\lim_\Lambda\frac{|C_\Lambda(t)|}{|\Lambda|}=0.
\]
Going back to~\eqref{eq:sosot} and using contractivity of the partial normalized
trace, we obtain, for any $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $t$ in a neighborhood of $0$,
\[
\lim_\Lambda\frac1{|\Lambda|}
\left|\nu(H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)-H_\Lambda(\Psi))\right|=0.
\]
In particular, the corresponding centered-cube limit vanishes. Combining this
with Part~\textbf{(iii)} of the \preSD{} property and
Theorem~\ref{thm:Gibbs}(i) gives
\[
\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^{-t}(E(\Psi))
=\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^{-t}(H_\Lambda(\Psi))
=\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}\nu(H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t))
=\nu(E(\Psi)).
\]
Thus a neighborhood of $0$ is contained in ${\mathcal T}_\Phi(E(\Psi))$ and it follows that
${\mathcal T}_\Phi(E(\Psi))={\mathbbm R}$. \hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:hc
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the group property of the dynamics, it suffices to show that~\eqref{eq:DynCommut}
holds for $t$ and $s$ in a neighborhood of $0$. Since $\Psi_t\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$ for small
enough $t$, it follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:Gibbs}(i), the \preSD{} property and
$E(\Psi)$ being a constant of the motion for $\tau_\Phi$ that,
for small enough $t$ and any $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$,
$$
\nu(E(\Psi_t))=\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}\nu(H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t))
=\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^{-t}(E(\Psi))=\nu(E(\Psi)).
$$
Proposition~\ref{prop:two-rpe}(v) thus gives $E(\Psi_t)\approx E(\Psi)$.
It then follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:phys-eq} that 
$\tau_{\Psi_t}=\tau_\Psi$, and Relation~\eqref{eq:Borodine} yields the statement.
\hfill$\Box$

label: SDplus
title: Definition
head: environment

label: thm:main2-const
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main2-const}
Let $\Phi,\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$ and suppose that $[\Psi]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$. If either
$(\Phi,\Psi)$ has the \preSDplus{} property or $\tau_\Phi$ preserves the
specific entropy, then for all $s,t\in{\mathbbm R}$, 
$$
\tau_\Phi^t \circ \tau_\Psi^s=\tau_\Psi^s\circ \tau_\Phi^t.
$$
head: environment

label: eq:pres-t
title: Proof
body_md:
We first assume that $(\Phi,\Psi)$ has the \preSDplus{} property.
By the group property, it suffices to show that $\alpha=\tau_\Psi$ for small
enough $t$. Although it may happen that $\Psi_t\not\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$,
the pressure and the specific energy associated with the local Hamiltonian family
$H(\Psi|\Phi,t)$ are well-defined. In the formulas below we denote these quantities,
with a slight abuse of notation, by $P(\Psi_t)$ and ${\mathcal e}_{\Psi_t}$. This is precisely
the local-Hamiltonian formalism used in the companion paper~\cite{Jaksic2026b}. It is immediate from the
definitions~\eqref{eq:PDef} and~\eqref{eq:ha-t} that
\begin{equation} 
P(\Psi_t)=P(\Psi),
\label{eq:pres-t}
\end{equation} 
while Part~\textbf{(iii)} of the \preSD{} property and $E(\Psi)$ being a constant of the motion for $\tau_\Phi$ 
ensure that for any $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ 
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal e}_{\Psi_t}(\omega)=
\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}\omega(H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t))=\lim_{\{\Lambda\}}\frac1{|\Lambda|}\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^{-t}(H_\Lambda(\Psi))
=\omega\circ\tau_\Phi^{-t}(E(\Psi))=\omega(E(\Psi))={\mathcal e}_{\Psi}(\omega).
\label{eq:energy-t} 
\end{equation}
We now appeal to Araki--Moriya's thermodynamic formalism. We shall use the terminology and
notation of~\cite{Araki2003} and refer the reader to this article for more details.
It follows from the \preSD{} property that $\Psi_t$ is a translation covariant general potential, 
as defined in~\cite[Section~5.5 and~8.1]{Araki2003}. More precisely, Conditions $(\Phi-\mathrm{a})$ 
and $(\Phi-\mathrm{b})$, \textsl{i.e.,\ } $\Psi_t(X)^\ast=\Psi_t(X)\in{\mathfrak A}_X$ for $X\in{\mathcal F}$, with 
$\Psi_t(\emptyset)=0$, are obviously satisfied. From the formula
$$
\Psi_t(X)=\sum_{Y\subset X}(-1)^{|X|-|Y|}H_Y(\Psi|\Phi,t)
$$
one easily infers Condition $(\Phi-\mathrm{f})$, translation covariance.
Condition $(\Phi-\mathrm{c})$, which expresses evenness in the fermionic
setting, is omitted for quantum spin systems. Finally, since for
$\Lambda\subset\Lambda'\in{\mathcal F}$,
$$
\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\subset\Lambda'}{X\cap\Lambda\neq\emptyset}}\Psi_t(X)
=H_{\Lambda'}(\Psi|\Phi,t)-H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\Psi|\Phi,t),
$$
it follows from Part~\textbf{(i)} of the \preSD{} property that
$$
\lim_{\Lambda'}\sum_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{1}{X\subset\Lambda'}{X\cap\Lambda\neq\emptyset}}\Psi_t(X)
=H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)+W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t),
$$
which yields Condition $(\Phi-\mathrm{e})$. Part~(ii) of the \preSD{} property
provides the surface-energy assumption of~\cite[Proposition~14.1]{Araki2003}.
Moreover, invariance of the trace under finite-volume unitary conjugation and
finite-range approximation in ${\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ give
$$
c=\lim_\Lambda\frac1{|\Lambda|}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits(H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t))
=\lim_\Lambda\frac1{|\Lambda|}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits(H_\Lambda(\Psi))=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\nolimits(E(\Psi)).
$$
By Part~(ii) of the \preSD{} property, the same trace limit is obtained with
$H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)+W_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)$ in place of
$H_\Lambda(\Psi|\Phi,t)$. Thus, \cite[Proposition~14.1]{Araki2003} applies:
there exists a translation covariant standard potential, \cite[Definition~5.10 and Section~8.1]{Araki2003} 
$\widetilde\Psi_t$ such that, for any $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$,
\begin{equation}
P(\widetilde\Psi_t)=P(\Psi_t)+c,\qquad {\mathcal e}_{\widetilde\Psi_t}(\omega)={\mathcal e}_{\Psi_t}(\omega)-c.
\label{eq:AMchanges}
\end{equation}
By~\cite[Section~11 and Proposition~14.1]{Araki2003}, Relations~\eqref{eq:pres-t}, \eqref{eq:energy-t} 
and~\eqref{eq:AMchanges} give that $\widetilde\Psi_t$, $\Psi_t$ and $\Psi$ share the same equilibrium states.
The \preSDplus{} property ensures that for $t$ in a neighborhood of $0$ the $C^\ast$-dynamics $\alpha=\tau_\Phi^{-t}\circ\tau_\Psi\circ\tau_\Phi^{t}$
satisfies properties~(II), (III) and~(IV) of~\cite[Section~1]{Araki2003}. It then follows 
from~\cite[Theorems~A and~B]{Araki2003} that $\tau_\Psi$ and $\alpha$ share the same KMS states. 
Hence, uniqueness of the modular group, Theorem~\ref{thm:israel}~\textbf{(iii)}, yields that
$\alpha=\tau_\Psi$ for small enough $t$.

Suppose now that $\tau_\Phi$ preserves the specific entropy. Choose
$\eta\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$.  Conservation of the specific entropy and the assumption
$[\Psi]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$ give, for all $t\in{\mathbbm R}$,
\[
s(\eta_t)-\eta_t(E(\Psi))
=s(\eta)-\eta(E(\Psi))=P(\Psi).
\]
Thus $\eta_t\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:KMSeq} implies that
$\eta_t$ is a $1$-KMS state for $\tau_\Psi$. By conjugation, $\eta_t$ is also a $1$-KMS state for
$\tau_\Phi^{-t}\circ\tau_\Psi\circ\tau_\Phi^t$. It follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:israel}~\textbf{(iii)} that
\[
\tau_\Phi^{-t}\circ\tau_\Psi^s\circ\tau_\Phi^t=\tau_\Psi^s
\]
for all $s,t\in{\mathbbm R}$. \hfill$\Box$

label: thm:jpst
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: eq:t-nice
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use a bilinear version of the argument in the proof
of~\cite[Theorem~2.8(2)]{Jaksic2023a}.

We first note that
\[
\sum_{X\ni0}\frac1{|X|}
\sum_{Y:\,Y\cap X\neq\emptyset}
\|[\Phi(Y),\Psi(X)]\|
\leq 2\|\Phi\|_{\mathrm s}\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm s},
\]
since $\sum_{Y:\,Y\cap X\neq\emptyset}\|\Phi(Y)\|
\leq |X|\|\Phi\|_{\mathrm s}$. The finite partial sums of
$E(\Psi)=\sum_{X\ni0}\Psi(X)/|X|$ belong to ${\mathfrak A}_\mathrm{loc}$ and converge
in norm. The estimate shows that their images under $\delta_\Phi$
also converge in norm. By closedness of $\delta_\Phi$, it follows that
$E(\Psi)\in\mathop{\mathrm{Dom}}\nolimits(\delta_\Phi)$ and that $\delta_\Phi(E(\Psi))$ is given
by the corresponding absolutely convergent commutator series.
Similarly, $E(\Phi)\in\mathop{\mathrm{Dom}}\nolimits(\delta_\Psi)$.

Fix $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$. Absolute convergence and translation invariance give
\begin{align*}
\nu(\delta_\Phi(E(\Psi)))
&=\sum_{X\ni0}\sum_{Y:\,Y\cap X\neq\emptyset}
\frac1{|X|\,|Y|}\sum_{y\in Y}
\nu\bigl(\mathrm{i}[\Phi(Y-y),\Psi(X-y)]\bigr)\\
&=\sum_{Y\ni0}\frac1{|Y|}
\sum_{X:\,X\cap Y\neq\emptyset}
\nu\bigl(\mathrm{i}[\Phi(Y),\Psi(X)]\bigr)\\
&=-\nu(\delta_\Psi(E(\Phi))).
\end{align*}
For the second equality, set $X'=X-y$ and $Y'=Y-y$. Then
$0\in Y'$ and $-y\in X'$. For each fixed pair $(X',Y')$, there
are exactly $|X'|$ possible values of $y$, cancelling the factor
$1/|X'|$.

Suppose now that $[\Psi]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$. Differentiating the conservation
identity at $t=0$ gives $\nu(\delta_\Phi(E(\Psi)))=0$ for every
$\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$. The preceding identity therefore yields
$\nu(\delta_\Psi(E(\Phi)))=0$ for every $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$.
Since $\nu\circ\tau_\Psi^t\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$, we obtain
\[
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t}\nu\circ\tau_\Psi^t(E(\Phi))
=(\nu\circ\tau_\Psi^t)(\delta_\Psi(E(\Phi)))=0.
\]
Thus $[\Phi]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Psi)$. The reverse implication follows by
interchanging $\Phi$ and $\Psi$. \hfill$\Box$

label: prop:wd-pres
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The pair $(\rho,\Psi)$ being regular, one has
$s(\nu|\rho)=-s(\nu)+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\nu)+P(\Psi)$ for all $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$.
Since $\tau_\Phi$ preserves the specific entropy, we further have
\begin{align*}
s(\nu|\rho)
&=-s(\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t)+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t)+P(\Psi)
+\nu\left(E(\Psi)-\tau_\Phi^t(E(\Psi))\right)
\\[4pt]
&=s(\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t|\rho)
+\nu\left(E(\Psi)-\tau_\Phi^t(E(\Psi))\right).
\end{align*}
Thus, \textbf{(i)} holds iff $E(\Psi)\approx\tau_\Phi^t(E(\Psi))$
for all $t\in{\mathbbm R}$. By the definition of ${\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$, this is precisely
\textbf{(ii)}. \hfill$\Box$

label: thm:main-cm-1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main-cm-1}
Suppose that $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ and let $\rho\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$.
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item If $\|\Psi\|_r<r$ for some $r>0$, then $(\rho,\Psi)$ is a regular pair
and there exists $T>0$ such that
\[
s(\nu \circ \tau_\Phi^t|\rho\circ\tau_\Phi^t)=s(\nu|\rho)
\]
for all $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $|t|<T$. If, in addition, $\rho$ is
$\tau_\Phi$-invariant, one can take $T=\infty$.
\item If $d=1$ and $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$, then $(\rho,\Psi)$ is a regular pair and
\[
s(\nu \circ \tau_\Phi^t|\rho\circ\tau_\Phi^t)=s(\nu|\rho)
\]
for all $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$.
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In Part~\textbf{(i)}, Theorem~\ref{thm:first-s}~\textbf{(iv)} gives
$\rho\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{wg}(\Psi)$, and hence $(\rho,\Psi)$ is regular. The assertion is
then Theorem~\ref{thm:pres-law}. Part~\textbf{(ii)} follows from
Theorems~\ref{thm:pre-ara} and~\ref{thm:pres-law-1}. \hfill$\Box$

label: thm:main-cm
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:KMSeq} , $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{KMS}(\Psi_+)$. 
Since $\omega_+$ is $\tau_\Phi$-invariant, it is 
also, for any fixed $s$, a $1$-KMS state for the $C^\ast$-dynamics 
$\tau_\Phi^s\circ\tau_{\Psi_+}\circ\tau_\Phi^{-s}$. It follows from 
Theorem~\ref{thm:israel}~\textbf{(iii)} that
\[
\tau_\Phi^s\circ\tau_{\Psi_+}^t\circ\tau_\Phi^{-s}=\tau_{\Psi_+}^t
\]
for all $s,t\in{\mathbbm R}$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:main1-const} yields the statement.\hfill$\Box$

label: thm-jpst2
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\omega_+$ is $\tau_\Phi$-invariant,
Theorem~\ref{thm:main-cm-1}~\textbf{(i)}, applied with $\rho=\omega_+$, holds for all
$t\in{\mathbbm R}$. Proposition~\ref{prop:wd-pres} then implies that
$[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$. Part~\textbf{(ii)} follows in the same way from
Theorem~\ref{thm:main-cm-1}~\textbf{(ii)}, applied with $\rho=\omega_+$. \hfill$\Box$

label: prop:DGVP-pot
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:DGVP-pot}
For any $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)$,
\[
s(\omega_+)\le s(\omega)+{\rm ep}_{\rm pot}(\omega).
\]
If $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ for some $\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ with
$[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$, then equality holds and $\Psi_+$ is a minimizer.
Under this assumption, $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ with $[\Psi]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$ is a minimizer
if and only if $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$. If, in addition,
$\Psi,\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$, this is equivalent to $\Psi\sim\Psi_+$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For any $[\Psi]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$, conservation of $E(\Psi)$ and the Gibbs variational principle give
\[
s_{\rm pot}(\omega|\Psi)
=-s(\omega)+{\mathcal e}_\Psi(\omega_+)+P(\Psi)
\ge s(\omega_+)-s(\omega).
\]
Taking the infimum over $\Psi$ gives the first assertion. If
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$, the Gibbs variational principle is saturated
at $\Psi_+$, and hence equality holds. Under this assumption, a
$\tau_\Phi$-invariant interaction $\Psi$ is a minimizer if and only if the Gibbs variational principle
is saturated at $\omega_+$, i.e., if and only if
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$. The last assertion follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:phys-eq}. \hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:fr
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:fr}
For any $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)$,
\[
\inf_{\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{req}(\Phi)}s(\omega|\nu)
\ge s(\omega_+)-s(\omega).
\]
If $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ for some $\Psi_+$ such that
$[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}_\mathrm{req}(\Phi)$, then equality holds and every
$\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ is a minimizer; in particular $\omega_+$ is a
minimizer. More generally, for $[\Psi]\in{\mathfrak C}_\mathrm{req}(\Phi)$ and
$\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$, the state $\nu$ attains the lower bound iff
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $[\Psi]\in{\mathfrak C}_\mathrm{req}(\Phi)$ and $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$. The regularity of
$(\nu,\Psi)$ gives that
\[
s(\omega|\nu)=-s(\omega)+{\mathcal e}_{\Psi}(\omega)+P(\Psi).
\]
Since $\Psi$ is $\tau_\Phi$-invariant, we further have
${\mathcal e}_{\Psi}(\omega)={\mathcal e}_{\Psi}(\overline\omega_T)$ for all $T>0$. Taking a
subsequence along which $\overline\omega_T\to\omega_+$ gives
\begin{align*}
s(\omega|\nu)
=-s(\omega)+{\mathcal e}_{\Psi}(\overline\omega_T)+P(\Psi)
\to&-s(\omega)+{\mathcal e}_{\Psi}(\omega_+)+P(\Psi)\nonumber\\
&=s(\omega_+|\nu)+s(\omega_+)-s(\omega)
\ge s(\omega_+)-s(\omega).
\end{align*}
For the fixed pair $(\nu,\Psi)$, equality holds iff
$s(\omega_+|\nu)=0$, equivalently iff
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$. The remaining assertions follow immediately.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:stein
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:stein}
Assume that ${\mathcal S}_{\mathrm{req},+}(\Phi)\neq\emptyset$.
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item For any $\omega_+,\omega_+'\in{\mathcal S}_{\mathrm{req},+}(\Phi)$,
$$
s(\omega_+)=s(\omega_+'),\qquad s(\omega_+'|\omega_+)=0.
$$
\item Fix $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_{\mathrm{req},+}(\Phi)$ and $\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{b}$ such that
$[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$, $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$, and
$(\nu,\Psi_+)$ is regular for every $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. Then
\[
{\mathcal S}_{\mathrm{req},+}(\Phi)\subset{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+).
\]
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For Part~\textbf{(i)}, choose a representative $\Psi_+$ of a class in
${\mathfrak C}_\mathrm{req}(\Phi)$ such that $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. Proposition~\ref{prop:fr}
gives
$s(\omega_+)=s(\omega_+')$. Since $[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$,
\[
{\mathcal e}_{\Psi_+}(\omega_+')={\mathcal e}_{\Psi_+}(\omega)={\mathcal e}_{\Psi_+}(\omega_+).
\]
Using regularity of $(\omega_+,\Psi_+)$ we therefore obtain
\[
s(\omega_+'|\omega_+)
=-s(\omega_+')+{\mathcal e}_{\Psi_+}(\omega_+')+P(\Psi_+)
=-s(\omega_+)+{\mathcal e}_{\Psi_+}(\omega_+)+P(\Psi_+)=0.
\]
This proves Part~\textbf{(i)}. 

For Part~\textbf{(ii)}, let $\omega_+'\in{\mathcal S}_{\mathrm{req},+}(\Phi)$. By
Part~\textbf{(i)}, $s(\omega_+'|\omega_+)=0$. 
Since $(\omega_+,\Psi_+)$ is regular, this is equivalent to
$\omega_+'\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. 
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop:DGVP-state
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:DGVP-state}
Let $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)\cap{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$ and choose
$\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}\cap{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{R}$ such that
$[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$ and $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. Then, the following hold.
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item
\[
\inf_{\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)}s(\omega|\nu)
=s(\omega_+)-s(\omega).
\]
\item The set of minimizers is precisely ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. In particular, the
minimizer is unique iff ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)=\{\omega_+\}$.
\item If $\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)\subset{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$ and
${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)=\{\omega_+\}$, then
$\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)=\{\omega_+\}$.
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)\subset{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{req}(\Phi)$, Proposition~\ref{prop:fr}
gives
\[
s(\omega|\nu)\ge s(\omega_+)-s(\omega)
\]
for $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$. Moreover, $[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}_\mathrm{req}(\Phi)$, and hence the same
proposition gives
\[
s(\omega|\omega_+)=s(\omega_+)-s(\omega).
\]
Since $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$, this proves Part~\textbf{(i)}.

Let $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$ be a minimizer and choose $\Psi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}\cap{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{R}$ such that $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$.
Equality in Proposition~\ref{prop:fr} gives $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi)$. Since
also $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$, Theorem~\ref{thm:phys-eq} yields
$\Psi\sim\Psi_+$ and therefore $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. Conversely, every
$\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ is a minimizer by Proposition~\ref{prop:fr}. This proves
Part~\textbf{(ii)}.

For Part~\textbf{(iii)}, let $\omega_+'\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)$. By assumption it belongs
to ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$, hence to ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{req}(\Phi)$. Proposition~\ref{prop:stein}(ii)
then gives $\omega_+'\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)=\{\omega_+\}$. \hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: def:ae
title: Definition
head: environment

label: prop:s-ha-2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:s-ha-2}
Suppose that $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)\cap{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ with
$\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$. If either \conjR{} and \conjSD{} both hold, or
\conjRplusSE{} holds, then $[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$ and
$\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{R}$, and consequently $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Under \conjR, $\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{R}$. Under \conjSD, the
pair $(\Phi,\Psi_+)$ has the \preSD{} property and
Theorem~\ref{thm:main-cm} gives $[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$. This proves the first
case.

If \conjRplusSE{} holds, then $\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{R}$ and, since a DSS is
$\tau_\Phi$-invariant, Relation~\eqref{eq:RplusSE} gives, for all
$\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{I}$ and $t\in{\mathbbm R}$,
\[
s(\nu\circ\tau_\Phi^t|\omega_+)=s(\nu|\omega_+).
\]
Proposition~\ref{prop:wd-pres} yields $[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$. \hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: prop-ruelle
title: Proposition
body_md:
Suppose that $\{\omega\}={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_0)$ for some $\Psi_0\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$.
If $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)\cap{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$, then
$s(\omega_+)>s(\omega)$.
\label{prop-ruelle}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that $s(\omega)=s(\omega_+)$ for some
$\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)\cap{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$. 
Since $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ with $[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$, we have
$\omega(E(\Psi_+))=\omega_+(E(\Psi_+))$, and the relation 
\[
s(\omega_+)=\omega_+(E(\Psi_+))+ P(\Psi_+)
\]
gives 
\[
s(\omega)=\omega(E(\Psi_+))+P(\Psi_+).
\]
Hence $\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. It follows that ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_0)\cap{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)\neq\emptyset$, 
and so ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_0)={\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:phys-eq}. Hence $\omega=\omega_+$ 
which contradicts our basic hypothesis that $\omega$ should not be $\tau_\Phi$-invariant.
\hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: def:fr-rol
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:fr-rol}
The pair $(\omega,\Phi)$ has the property of \textsl{finite-range restoration
of locality} if every $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)$ belongs to
${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$ for some $\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$.
head: environment

label: thm:fr-rol-1d
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:fr-rol-1d}
Suppose that $d=1$, that $\Phi,\Psi_0\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$, that
$\omega\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_0)$, and that $(\omega,\Phi)$ has the property of
finite-range restoration of locality. Then the following hold:
\begin{romanenumerate}
\item $\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)=\{\omega_+\}$.
\item for any $\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ such that $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$, one 
has $[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$ and $\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{R}$. 
\item the dynamical Gibbs variational principle holds and $\omega_+$ is its
unique minimizer.
\item $s(\omega_+)>s(\omega)$.
\end{romanenumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\nu\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)$. By finite-range restoration of
locality, $\nu\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_\nu)$ for some $\Psi_\nu\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:jpst}~\textbf{(ii)}, the pair $(\Phi,\Psi_\nu)$ has the \preSD{}
property, and it follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:main-cm} 
that $[\Psi_\nu]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:pre-ara}, ${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_\nu)$ 
is a singleton and its unique element is weak Gibbs, hence regularity holds. 
Thus $[\Psi_\nu]\in\mathfrak{C}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$ and $\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)\subset{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$.

Fix $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)$ and a corresponding
$\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$. Theorem~\ref{thm:pre-ara} gives
${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)=\{\omega_+\}$, while Proposition~\ref{prop:DGVP-state}~(iii) yields
Part~\textbf{(i)}. Parts~\textbf{(ii)} and~\textbf{(iii)} follow from the preceding 
argument and Proposition~\ref{prop:DGVP-state}. Finally,
${\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_0)=\{\omega\}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:pre-ara}, and Part~\textbf{(iv)} follows
from Proposition~\ref{prop-ruelle}. \hfill$\Box$
head: manual

label: def:ate
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:ate}
The pair $(\omega,\Phi)$ has the property of \textsl{approach to thermal
equilibrium} if
\[
\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)\subset{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\omega,\Phi).
\]
head: environment

label: thm:fr-ate
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:fr-ate}
Suppose that $\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ and that $(\omega,\Phi)$ has the property of
finite-range restoration of locality. If
\[
{\mathfrak C}_{{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}}(\Phi)\coloneq{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)\cap[{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}]=\operatorname{span}\{[\Phi]\},
\]
then $(\omega,\Phi)$ has the property of approach to thermal equilibrium.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\omega_+\in\Sigma_+(\omega,\Phi)$ and choose
$\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{f}$ such that $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:jpst}~\textbf{(ii)} and Theorem~\ref{thm:main-cm}, 
$[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$. Hence $[\Psi_+]=\lambda[\Phi]$ for some
$\lambda\in{\mathbbm R}$. Since ${\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega_+)={\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)$, the 
definition of the equilibrium inverse temperature gives $\lambda=\beta_\mathrm{eq}$. 
Thus $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\omega,\Phi)$. \hfill$\Box$

body_md:
Suppose first that $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\omega,\Phi)$. Then
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi)$. Since $E(\Phi)$ is a constant of the
motion and $\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}\cap{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{R}$, it follows that
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$.

Conversely, assuming that $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{phys}(\Phi)$, one can choose 
$\Psi_+\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}\cap{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{R}$ such that $[\Psi_+]\in{\mathfrak C}(\Phi)$ and
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. By the assumption on $\omega_\mathrm{eq}$ and
conservation of $E(\Psi_+)$,
\[
\omega_\mathrm{eq}(E(\Psi_+))
=\omega(E(\Psi_+))
=\omega_+(E(\Psi_+)).
\]
Hence
\begin{align*}
0\le s(\omega_\mathrm{eq}|\omega_+)
&=-s(\omega_\mathrm{eq})+\omega_\mathrm{eq}(E(\Psi_+))+P(\Psi_+)\\[1mm]
&=s(\omega_+)-s(\omega_\mathrm{eq}).
\end{align*}
Proposition~\ref{prop:st-pres} gives the reverse inequality, and therefore
$s(\omega_\mathrm{eq}|\omega_+)=0$. Regularity of $(\omega_+,\Psi_+)$ yields
$\omega_\mathrm{eq}\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\Psi_+)$. Since also
$\omega_\mathrm{eq}\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi)$ and
$\Psi_+,\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi\in{\mathcal B}_\mathrm{sd}$, Theorem~\ref{thm:phys-eq} gives $\Psi_+\sim\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi$. 
It follows that $\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\beta_\mathrm{eq}\Phi)$. Finally,
${\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega_+)={\mathcal e}_\Phi(\omega)$ by energy conservation, and hence
$\omega_+\in{\mathcal S}_\mathrm{eq}(\omega,\Phi)$.\vskip-8pt \hfill$\Box$
